| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | Cambridge-wide policy applied at journal level: AI tools cannot be listed as author (accountability requirement not met by AI). Declaration required if AI used to generate text/images/translations or to analyze/extract insights from data, with tool name/version, access info, and dates disclosed (acknowledgments/footnote for text, methods section for data analysis, figure captions for visuals). Minor uses (spelling/grammar check, single words/brief phrases, formatting) do not require declaration. This is the general CUP author-instructions page for this journal, not a Religious-Studies-specific policy statement -- CUP's central AI ethics policy (2023) applies across ~400 journals. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/religious-studies/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Analytic philosophy of religion and philosophical theology: problem of evil/theodicy (existentialist and classical framings), divine attributes (omnipotence, omniscience), apophatic theology, epistemology of theistic belief, miracles, prayer and time, science-engaged theology, and philosophy of religion drawing on non-Western/non-Christian traditions (2025 special issues covered Afro-Brazilian religions and Latin American philosophy of religion; forthcoming Feb 2026 special issue on Theology Meets Philosophy of Science; a 2025 special issue on Experimental Philosophy of Religion signals openness to empirically-informed methods).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** analytic/conceptual argumentation, phenomenological analysis, engagement with classical theological/philosophical traditions, science-engaged theology (dialogue with physics, biology, neuroscience), experimental philosophy of religion (per Sept 2025 special issue), comparative/non-Western philosophy of religion (e.g., Afro-Brazilian, Latin American traditions per 2025 special issues)

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**Sources cited across this entry:**
- WebSearch result listing 2025-2026 special issues (Experimental Philosophy of Religion Sept 2025; Afro-Brazilian Religions July 2025; Latin America God's existence June 2025; Theology Meets Philosophy of Science Feb 2026)
- https://scirev.org/journal/religious-studies/ (WebFetch, SciRev aggregate stats -- appears to reflect a very small number of logged reviews, likely 1-2)
- https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/religious-studies/information/about-this-journal (WebSearch/WebFetch, aims and scope)
- https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/religious-studies/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials
- https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/religious-studies/latest-issue (WebFetch, Vol 62 Issue 2, June 2026 table of contents)

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **peer_review.type**: Cambridge Core 'about this journal' and author-instructions pages state the journal uses Manuscript Central / an Online Peer Review Service (OPRS) but do not disclose whether review is single-blind, double-blind, or open; the dedicated 'Peer review information' subpage returned HTTP 404 on fetch attempt, and no search result surfaced the specific model.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: SciRev page explicitly lists this as n/a for this journal (sample too small); no forum or cross-language source discussed desk-reject rates for this specific journal.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No first-hand discussion found on 小木虫 muchong.com, 知乎 zhihu, fabiaoji-family sites (letpub rate-limited on fetch, other fabiao sites returned only generic journal-directory listings), or Reddit r/AskAcademia describing reviewer tone/culture for this specific journal -- only generic journal-info aggregator pages surfaced, which do not count as experiential.
- **preprint.source_url**: The general 'preparing your materials' author-instructions page states preprints are allowed on personal sites/institutional repositories/preprint archives subject to Cambridge's general Preprint Policy, but no Religious-Studies-specific preprint policy page was found distinct from the boilerplate Cambridge Core policy language.

**Cross-language checks performed (mandatory per methodology):**
- 小木虫 muchong.com -- WebSearch for "muchong.com \"Religious Studies\" 期刊" returned 0 relevant results (only unrelated Chinese journal-directory sites for other titles like Religions/MDPI, Journal for the Study of Religions and Ideologies)
- 知乎 zhihu -- WebSearch for "zhihu \"Religious Studies\" 期刊 投稿" returned only tangential zhuanlan articles listing SSCI journals in anthropology/sociology of religion and a haoqikan.com directory page; no first-hand submitter accounts
- fabiaoji-family sites (letpub.com.cn, sfabiao/haofabiao/haoqikan/yunzazhi) -- letpub.com.cn page for this ISSN was found but WebFetch was rate-limited (Chinese error: IP requesting too frequently); other fabiao-family results were generic journal-metric directory pages with no submitter experience narrative
- Reddit r/AskAcademia -- WebSearch "site:reddit.com \"Religious Studies\" journal desk reject philosophy religion" returned 0 results; broader WebSearch also surfaced no relevant Reddit threads
